summary: Semiconductors, LEDs, transistors, capacitors, transformers, regulators, diodes, SCRs, TRIACs, crystals and relays.

blocks.title: Semiconductors and light
items: Heat or light frees electrons, each leaving a hole: 2 charge carriers.
Photoconductive effect: light raises conductivity, so resistance falls.
Photovoltaic effect: light becomes EMF directly, as in a solar cell.
Doping gives N-type (extra electrons) and P-type (extra holes), meeting at a PN junction.

blocks.title: LEDs
items: LED (light-emitting diode): forward bias only. Materials set the color; current sets brightness.
20 mA: operating current and safe maximum. Needs a series resistor.
Optoisolator or optocoupler: LED and photosensitive device, light-tight. Optointerrupter: an open slot.

items.name: Alpha, beta
items.means: Alpha, collector vs emitter: just under 1, 0.95 to 0.995. Beta, collector vs base: about 20 to several hundred. Beta cutoff: emitter current gain down to 0.707 of maximum.

blocks.title: MOSFETs and CMOS
items: MOSFET: metal-oxide semiconductor field-effect transistor. Gate voltage controls the channel; thin oxide insulates the gate.
CMOS: complementary metal-oxide semiconductor, P-channel and N-channel MOSFETs paired.
Static charges damage FET and CMOS parts.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Diode types: junction and point contact. Electrolytic is a capacitor.
Highest DC resistance: the 150 V winding, most turns.
A FET has a drain, not a sink.
